result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Pipeline]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass} | Pointblank description: Enforce data contracts at both ends of a data transformation. twitter-card: title: >- [Pipeline]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass} | Pointblank description: Enforce data contracts at both ends of a data transformation. title: "[Pipeline]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Enforce data contracts at both ends of a data transformation. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Enforce data contracts at both ends of a data transformation. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/pipeline.py#L280-L1441){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-class} ```pythonsignature Pipeline( source=None, target=None, thresholds=None, actions=None, final_actions=None, label=None, short_circuit=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Most data problems are introduced at a boundary: an upstream system starts sending nulls or a new category, or a transformation step drops, duplicates, or miscalculates rows. A `Pipeline` guards those boundaries. It pairs a *source* [`Contract`](`pointblank.Contract`), describing the data a transformation expects to receive, with a *target* contract, describing the data it promises to produce. Data is validated against the source contract on the way in and against the target contract on the way out, so a failure tells you whether the input was bad or the transformation went wrong. The pipeline doesn't run or schedule your transformation logic beyond calling the function you give it. The transformation can use any DataFrame library, and the pipeline can sit inside any orchestration tool. You can also check just one boundary with [`validate_source()`](`pointblank.Pipeline.validate_source`) or [`validate_target()`](`pointblank.Pipeline.validate_target`), for example when the transformation runs somewhere else. Only one of the two contracts is required, so a pipeline can also act as an ingestion guard (source only) or an output guard (target only). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Contract | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The [`Contract`](`pointblank.Contract`) that incoming data must meet. Leave it as `None` for a pipeline that only checks output. [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Contract | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The [`Contract`](`pointblank.Contract`) that the transformed data must meet. Leave it as `None` for a pipeline that only checks input. At least one of `source=` and `target=` must be given. [thresholds]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Thresholds | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : [`Thresholds`](`pointblank.Thresholds`) to use for both boundary validations. When given, they replace each contract's own `thresholds=` (they aren't merged), which lets the same contracts be applied more or less strictly in different settings. Thresholds set on individual steps still take precedence. Thresholds determine the warning, error, and critical levels shown in the reports and the [`Actions`](`pointblank.Actions`) they trigger, but not whether a boundary passes (see *Passing and Failing* below). [actions]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Actions | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : [`Actions`](`pointblank.Actions`) to take when a step in either boundary validation reaches a threshold level. The same actions are used for both boundaries. [final_actions]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [FinalActions | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : [`FinalActions`](`pointblank.FinalActions`) to run when a boundary validation finishes. They run once for each boundary that's validated, so twice in a full run. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A label for the pipeline. Each boundary validation is labeled `"
